Matters relating to General Elections
3.14 On the issue of remuneration to observers engaged during elections, the Election Commission
in it’s replies to the questionnaire had informed that the Commission considered the matter of granting
a lump sum of Rs. l5,000/- in the form of honorarium after successful completion of his/her duty
in an election. The Commission justified the need for a handsome remuneration since Observers were
normally required to report to the constituency one to two days before the last date of nomination
and stay till the poll/repoll is completed, required to make their second visit to the constituency to
oversee the process of counting of votes, that they are required to make sure that the poll is
conducted smoothly and work in a non-partisan manner, ensure that there is no violation of the Model
Code of Conduct and maintain the purity of the process and activities required for conduct of poll.
3.15 The Committee welcomes the proposal of granting an attractive honorarium to observers
engaged during elections. It also desires that these officials may be given precise and complete
training on the responsibilities bestowed upon them so that they may function more efficiently.
As regards complaints under the Model Code of Conduct, the Committee urges that these may
be verified before cases are filed against candidates.
Model Code of Conduct
3.16 Members were also of the considered view that some contents of the Model Code of Conduct,
such as, the jurisdiction of applicability of the Code especially when elections were held not in the
entire State, the mode of filing cases against candidates/parties on charges of violation of the Code
of Conduct, the extent of publicity and broadcast during elections amongst many others call for a
thorough review. In this context, the Committee recommends that the recommendations of the
All-Party Committee on Electoral Reforms which submitted its report in May 1990, on the
subject matter may be taken into consideration.
3.17 The Committee observes that Model Code of Conduct is a voluntary agreement between
the parties for regulating the conduct of political parties and its members etc., during the process
of elections to Assemblies and Parliament. Its legal status is a grey area. After hearing the views
of the officials of the Ministry of Law and considering the problems which have erupted in the
country, from time to time, in the last few years, the Committee feels that the Code, which was
voluntary in nature at one time has not remained so after insertion of para 16A in the Election
Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968, which authorises the Election Commission, to
suspend or withdraw the recognition of political parties in case of violation of Code of Conduct.
Besides, some of the paras in the code attract penal provisions in other laws.
3.18 The Committee further observes that the power of cancellation of registration of a
political party is substantive in nature and, therefore, should not be regulated or provided for

15
under an “Order” of the Commission. It should either be a part of the Representation of
Peoples Act, 1951 or the Rules framed there under. Further, the scope of Article 324 also needs
to be examined as, many of the aspects which should have been covered under the Rules
framed under R.P. Act 1951 are presently covered under instructions issued under Article 324
of the Constitution by the Commission.
3.19 Accordingly, in Committee’s view, remedial legal steps are required to be taken in this
regard.

3.22 Amidst all the drawbacks that exist, the Committee notes with appreciation the impressive
EPIC coverage of the States. It, however, feels that unless 100% coverage is achieved, the
intent of the scheme is not realized. Moreover, it also constitutes a denial of the right to
franchise to those not covered by the scheme. Therefore, the Committee impresses upon the
Commission to take all-out effort for 100% EPIC coverage of the States in a time-bound
manner. It also suggests that the funds may be enhanced, if needed, so that the resources
could be strengthened to accomplish the task in the minimum time span.
3.23 The Committee also puts on record it’s appreciation for the transparency that the
Election Commission of India has brought into the electoral system in the country. There has
been good progress in making the elections transparent, although there is still much scope for
doing more. Acknowledging that Electoral Reforms being too vast a subject for a one-time re-
look, the Committee suggests that the Commission may invite suggestions from all sections
of the population and initiate a streamlining process.

Electronic Voting Machine
3.24 An amount of Rs.113.92 crores sanctioned in the financial year 2010-2011 for settling
outstanding bills of 1 lac EVMs and 27000 Ballot units purchased in 2009. During the financial years
2010-11 and 2011-12, no EVMs have been procured.
3.25 During the course of discussion in the meeting some of the Members expressed that the
EVM’s are not trustworthy and tamperable. Most of the developed countries like USA are not using
the EVM’s in their general elections. Members expressed their reservation with regard to the transparency
in the votes by EVM. Some Members stated that a voter is not sure that his/her vote has gone to
the candidate of his choice as he does not receive any visual impression as on paper assuring him/
her that his vote was rightly cast.
3.26 The Director General, Election Commission while deposing before the Committee explained that:
“...as soon as the voter presses the button, red light glows against the symbol of the candidate
whose button the voter presses. This is the confirmation that the vote has been cast in favour
of the said candidate. For the information and confidence of the candidates and the parties,
a mock poll is conducted before the actual poll on the polling day in which, the candidates
or their agents are allowed to cast about 100 votes and thereafter the same votes are counted
before them and tallied and this way the trustworthiness of the EVM is established even before
the actual polling takes place. After the mock poll, the voter recorded in the EVMs during
the mock poll are erased before the actual poll and this also is shown to the candidates or
their agents by pressing the button which shows that the votes already recorded is zero” .
3.27 The Committee acknowledges the explanation given by the Election Commission and
the Legislative Department. The Committee feels EVMs are very much needed in a vast
democratic country like ours and have been used effectively in the elections in the country.
The lacunae pointed out by Members in the machine, needs to be looked into and removed
to repose complete trust in the voter. In this context, the Committee desires that a detailed
note on the status of reliability of EVMs may be furnished to the Committee at the time of
furnishing ATRs.

activities of the human life are covered by some law or the other. When some persons,
especially, the deprived persons and marginalised persons, living in far-off places face
difficulties in getting things done even by officers of the Executive, it also becomes a problem
of access to justice. So, we have expanded our activities. We have had a paradigm shift in
this matter by making this legal aid concept to slowly move away from the provision of
providing advocates to the needy persons to taking the legal services to the door-step of the
people. We have developed a new technique to bring the people in need of legal services to
the legal service institutions.”

4.21 The paradigm shift in the interpretation of “legal services” in the Legal Services
Authorities Act and moving towards taking legal services to the door-step of the people is a
welcome approach. The Committee commends this progressive concept of the NALSA. While

5.13 The Committee was informed that the Representation of the People (Amendment) Bill, 2006,
introduced in the Rajya Sabha on the 17 th February, 2006 sought to amend Section 20 of the
Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950) to make provision for enabling the Indian
Citizens, absenting from their place of ordinary residence in India owing to their employment,
education or otherwise outside India, to get their names registered in the electoral rolls of the
concerned constituency of their place of ordinary residence in India, had they been in India, so that
they would be in a position to cast their votes in the elections to the Lok Sabha and to the State
Legislatures in case they happen to be in their constituency at the time of the polls.
5.14 The above mentioned Bill was referred to the Department Related Parliamentary Standing
Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice on the 27 th March, 2006 for examination
and report. The Committee presented its 16 th report on the subject to both the Houses of Parliament.
In its Report  the Committee, while agreeing with the letter and spirit of the amendment Bill, has
recommended for bringing a comprehensive Bill on the subject containing all the details regarding the
manner of enrolment of the Non-Resident Indians, the mode of voting and the conditionalities for
contesting elections.
5.15 On the basis of the recommendations of the Hon’ble Standing Committee the aforesaid Bill was
withdrawn and a fresh Bill, namely, the Representation of the People (Amendment) Bill 2010 was
introduced in the Parliament on the 20 th August, 2010. The said Bill after getting passed by both the
Houses of Parliament was enacted as the Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 2010 (36
of 2010).

Registration of the Electors Rules, 1960, has been amended vide the Registration of Electors
(Amendment) Rules, 2011, which has been notified in the Gazette of India on the 2 nd February, 2011.

2011, on 23 rd February, 2011 so as to enable publication of the rolls on the website of the Chief
Electoral Officer of the concerned State as well as to submit the application for registration accompanied

abroad.

CENTRALLY SPONSORED SCHEME RELATING TO INFRASTRUCTURAL FACILITIES FOR
THE JUDICIARY
6.6 Inadequacy of infrastructure facilities in District and Subordinate courts has remained a major
bottleneck in the judicial system largely contributing to the accumulation of arrears. In order to
augment the resources of the State Governments for development of infrastructure facilities for the
judiciary, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) has been in operation since 1993-94. During Regional
Consultations at Guwahati, Chennai, Kolkata, New Delhi and Goa between June-August, 2010, several
States raised the demand for change in the funding pattern of the CSS from 50:50 to 75:25
and enhancement of the amount of Central grant. Accordingly, the Centre-State sharing ratio for
North-Eastern States has been changed to 90:10 and for other States to 75:25 with effect from
2011-12.
6.7 An amount of Rs. 526.55 crore has been released under the Scheme to States/UTs till
February, 2012 out of a total of Rs. 623.43 crore made available in RE in 2011-12. A provision of
Rs. 660 crore has been kept for Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the financial year 2012-13.
6.8 The Committee was also informed that the inclusion of furnishing of courts and other facilities
under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the development of infrastructure facilities for the judiciary
is under consideration of Department of Justice.

37

the Planning Commission for the Eleventh Plan period (2007-12). The expenditure in the first four
years of 11
th Plan was Rs. 554.71 crore, on the scheme. Considering the demands from State
Governments for improvement of infrastructure of subordinate judiciary, the allocation for infrastructure
has substantially increased to Rs. 542.90 crore in the last year of the Plan period i.e. 2011-12, which
was further increased to Rs. 623.43 crore at RE stage. An amount of Rs. 595.74 crore has been
released to States/UTs under this Scheme during last financial year (2011-12).

infrastructure for subordinate judiciary and the total requirement for the fund comes to the tune of

requirement would be met by the Central Government. Roughly an amount of Rs. 5000 crores will

subsequent years.

infrastructure for subordinate judiciary. Accordingly, a provision of Rs. 660 crore has been kept for
the Scheme during the first year of 12

NATIONAL MISSION FOR JUSTICE DELIVERY AND LEGAL REFORMS
6.16 The Government having approved, the setting up of a National Mission for Justice Delivery
and Legal Reforms in June, 2011, had decided in June, 2011 to operationalize the same to ensure a
well-coordinated response of the executive and the judiciary for speeding up delivery of justice in the
country and to reduce the delay in the disposal of cases by the courts. At the same time, the National
Mission will work towards ensuring that the quality of justice imparted to the citizens is maintained
at the desire high levels providing access to justice for the marginalised sections of the society.
6.17 The Committee was informed that the National Mission would focus on two major goals as
envisaged in the Vision Document 2009, namely: (i) increasing access by reducing delays and arrears
in the system, and (ii) enhancing accountability through structural changes, and by setting performance
standards and capacities.
6.18 Five strategic initiatives proposed under the Mission are Policy and Legislative changes, re-
engineering procedures and alternate methods of Dispute Resolution, Human Resource Development,
leveraging ICT for better justice delivery and improved infrastructure for district and subordinate
judiciary. The National Mission period coinciding almost with the 12
th Plan, provides a platform for
addressing some of the factors affecting performance of the judiciary in effective justice delivery.
(i) National Mission-Action Plan Implementation:
6.19 The activities under the tentative Action Plan of the National Mission are explained in brief as under:
(a) Policy and legislative changes such as All India Judicial Service, Litigation Policy, Judicial
Impact Assessment, Amendment in the N.I. Act and the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
Legal Education Reforms, etc.
(b) Re-engineering procedures and alternate methods of Dispute Resolution such as identification
of bottlenecks, procedural changes in court processes, statutory amendments to reduce
and disincentives delays, Fast tracking of procedures, appointment of court managers and
Alternate Dispute Resolution, etc.
(c) Focus on Human Resource Development such as strengthening State Judicial Academies,
Training of Public Prosecutors and strengthening National Judicial Academy and Training
of mediators.
6.20 In order to carry-out above mentioned activities for implementation of the Action Plan of the
Mission, a provision of Rs.20.00 crore has been made under B.E. 2012-13 for effective implementation
of various initiatives to be undertaken by the National Mission.

40
(ii) Setting up of Model Courts (Phase-I)
6.21 This is a new Scheme proposed in the 12 th Five Year Plan to cover the gaps in the existing
schemes and policies and with a view to demonstrate change in a scenario where end to end needs
for judicial reform are met, it is proposed to implement a pilot Project in select subordinate (Model)
courts. This will imply that not only court rooms but select court premises are made IT-enabled to
allow e-flow of information from filing of a case to pronouncement of a judgement. Not only judicial
officers, but the entire court staff is trained to impart service delivery. Court and cases management
principles shall be adopted in these courts that adhere to pre-decided timelines that are also shared with
the lawyers in advance. Judicial academies are supported not just with funds for training, but also to
develop research abilities and retain permanent and competent faculty. An innovative experiment is also
proposed to be supported in select Union Territory to implement and end to end criminal justice reform
ensuring that the police, prosecution, judiciary and prison work to their best of ability. For the purpose
explained above a budget provision of Rs.7.5 crore is proposed.
6.22 The Secretary (Justice) during his deposition before the Committee on the Demands for Grants
(2012-13) informed the Committee that the Scheme has been proposed in the light of the current
scenario of disposal of cases. He stated that 2.77 crore cases are pending in Subordinate Courts
comprising of 70% Criminal cases and 29% Civil cases, 42.49 lakhs cases are pending in High Courts
comprising of 21% Criminal cases and 79% Civil cases and a total of 54,612 cases are pending in
the Supreme Court.
6.23 The Secretary further informed that 60% of the disposal of cases depends on the Judge while
the rest 40% depend on case management, Court management, infrastructural facilities and enabling
environment.
6.24 The Committee welcomes the new instrument of service, namely, “National Mission for
Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms” which is aimed at tackling major core problematic issues
of Judiciary. The Committee is appreciative that the scheme has been designed to ensure the
much needed coordination between the executive and the judiciary, which, it is certain will
result in a much more efficient delivery of justice in the country.
6.25 The Committee is given to understand through the Outcome Budget (2012-13) of the
Ministry that no timeline has been fixed for the implementation of this Scheme. It is, however,
of the view that it is pertinent to impose timeline in the Action Plan on certain aspects of the
Scheme, such as, setting up of Project Management Units, consultation with stakeholders or
proposed studies on the various aspects of the judicial reforms. The Committee feels that the
experience with many Schemes launched by the Government face set-backs after its
implementation for two or three years due to absence of a strict timeline and ends up clogged
in logjams of non-receipt of UCs and thereafter leading to unutilised funds. The same has been
in the case with the schemes of setting up of Family Courts, Gram Nyayalayas and the projects
under the Centrally Sponsored Schemes. Therefore, the Committee recommends that clear
targets and timelines may be drawn and very close monitoring and regular appraisal should be
made to ensure the successful implementation of the Scheme.

th Finance Commission. The Committee however, feels that

the organisations. Also, their expertise would be utilised to the maximum benefit if the

6.71 An appraisal of the vacancy position of Judges in both Supreme Court and High Courts
as provided by the Department is disheartening. One major factor affecting these vacancies

process of appointment is set right, other related issues, such as court management and
pendency of cases will fall in place. The Department is, accordingly exhorted to take efficacious
steps in this domain.

adjudication of cases. Shortage of judges is also a major constraint for setting up of new
courts. The Committee appreciates and welcomes idea of having in place an All India Judicial
Service but, in case, certain States have issues in this proposal, the Committee feels that the
Central Government can at least make a beginning by holding an examination for recruiting
judges at the all India level, covering States that agree to participate or accept candidates
selected on the basis of the said recruitment. The Committee feels such a move would ensure
an all time availability of qualified and deserving candidates for appointment in subordinate
courts.

7.0 Demand No. 63 in the detailed Demands of Grants of the Ministry of Law and Justice pertains
to the Supreme Court of India. The expenditure to be incurred on the Supreme Court of India is
‘Charged’. The total Budget Estimates of the Supreme Court of India for the year 2010-11  is Rs. 85
crore as against Rs. 100.69 crore in Revised Estimates for the year 2009-10.
7.1. The Committee had recommended in its earlier Reports to establish the Constitutional Bench
and other Benches of the Supreme Court given the manifold benefits of this exercise. The Law
Commission in its 229th Report had also expressed the same opinion regarding the establishment of
other Benches of the Supreme Court. However, in its reply to the questionnaire of the Committee,
Ministry acquainted the Committee that to implement the Committee’s recommendations, wide ranging
amendments are needed in the Constitution. Moreover, the Ministry also informed that having considered
the matter in the meeting of the Full Court, the Chief Justice of India finds no justification for
establishing the other Benches of the Supreme Court. Therefore, the Ministry did not intend to pursue
the matter further.

53
7.2 The Committee is not in agreement with the Ministry and the opinion of the Chief
Justice of India as well. The Committee feels that unwillingness regarding establishment of the
other Benches of the Supreme Court cannot be justified on the grounds that it would attract
a cumbersome process of constitutional amendment. The Committee also feels that such an
amendment is the need of the hour and would prove to be a step in the right direction to
make the Higher Courts accessible to all the regions of the country. The Committee feels that
the Constitution of India is a living document and has enough scope to accommodate the
demands arising out in a changed milieu in view of the provisions under Article 130 that
read -
“The Supreme Court sits in Delhi. It can, however, meet in any other place or places as
the Chief Justice may, with the approval of the President.”
7.3 The Committee, therefore, reiterates the need for establishment of benches of the
Supreme Court as it would be of immense help to the poor who cannot afford to travel from
their native places to Delhi.
7.4 The Committee in its earlier Reports recommended that the Supreme Court journals containing
all important judgments’ and cases should be publicised and commercialised to get wider publicity and
even unreported cases should also get reference in the journals. The Committee had also recommended
different High Courts of the country to also publicize and commercialize their judgments and cases
through their journals and make reference of unreported cases. The Committee was apprised that the
abovementioned recommendations had been forwarded to the Supreme Court Registry for necessary
action. The Committee was further apprised, that in pursuance of the Committee’s recommendations
the reported judgments of the High Courts and Supreme Court are available on their respective
websites.
7.5 The Committee appreciates that the Ministry has replied in affirmative and forwarded
the abovementioned Committee’s recommendations to the Supreme Court Registry for necessary
action. The Committee hopes that the Supreme Court Registry would positively take decisions
in this regard.
7.6 The Committee in its earlier Reports had also recommended measures to strengthen the
financial resources of the Supreme Court and High Courts and to enable the Supreme Court and High
Courts to generate Revenue themselves which can also be utilised by the Subordinate Judiciary. The
Committee was apprised that the Department is in agreement with the views of the Committee.
However, the Department apprised that the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance was the
controlling authority for financial and budgetary matters in respect of the Supreme Court and for the
High Courts the State Governments are the controlling authority for financial and budgetary matters.
Thus final decision in this regard lies at their end.
7.7 The Committee is pleased to note that the Department is in agreement with the
Committee’s recommendation regarding enabling the Supreme Court and High Courts to
generate Revenue themselves which can also be utilised by the Subordinate Judiciary. The
Committee would, however, appreciate if the Department pursues the matter with the Department
of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance and the State Governments to consider the matter
expeditiously. The Committee may be apprised their feedback, accordingly.
PENDENCY OF CASES
7.8 In response to the queries raised by the Hon’ble members, the Registrar Supreme Court while
deposing before the Committee during the deliberations on the Demand for Grants 2010-11 put light
on the matter of pendency of cases as follows.

54
“...Definitely, the Supreme Court is taking various steps to see that the pendency of cases is
brought down and the cases are decided within a time frame. There are various reasons which
prevent us from doing so. Mainly, it is because of the deficiencies in the infrastructure; funding
is also a problem; number of Judges is also a problem; and, various complex matters come
before the various courts in India. We do feel that increase in the number of cases shows the
increased faith in the judicial system. Sir, till about 4-5 years back, the number of disposals
in the Supreme Court was higher than the number of institutions. But for the past few years,
the cases have increased and with the number of Judges remaining the same, the disposal ratio
of each Judge has gone up. So, we attribute increase in the pendency of cases mainly to the
increase in the number of cases. That can be the only reason. It is true that it has increased.”
7.9 The Committee expresses it serious concerns over the huge pendency of cases in
Higher Courts. Taking into account the reasons cited by the Registrar, Supreme Court in this
regard, the Committee feels that the problem is not being addressed seriously and wholehearted
efforts are yet to be made to deal with the problem. The Committee is of the view that both
Executive and Judiciary should work in tandem to deal with the adversities arising out of
mounting pendency. As far as the need of more judges is concerned, the Committee reiterates
its earlier recommendation that the vacancies of judges in the High Court should be expeditiously
filled up. The Government should vigorously pursue the matter with the Chief Justice of the
High Courts for necessary actions.

per the demands projected while there exist a meager shortfall in the Non-Plan allocation.

Ministry of Finance to take austerity measures in expenditure, it is also of the considered view

compromised. The Committee, during it’s interaction with the various autonomous bodies and
institutions under the Ministry’s administrative control, was informed of the shortage of funds
thereby adversely affecting their performance. In that backdrop, the Committee hopes that the
Ministry will be judicious in the utilisation of the budgetary allocation. [Para 2.5]

increase in the Plan and Non-Plan budgetary allocations for the year 2012-13 as against 2011-12.

Matters relating to General Elections
6. The Committee welcomes the proposal of granting an attractive honorarium to observers
engaged during elections. It also desires that these officials may be given precise and complete
training on the responsibilities bestowed upon them so that they may function more efficiently.
As regards complaints under the Model Code of Conduct, the Committee urges that these may

7. In this context, the Committee recommends that the recommendations of the All-Party
Committee on Electoral Reforms which submitted its report in May, 1990, on the subject
matter may be taken into consideration. [Para 3.16]
8. The Committee observes that Model Code of Conduct is a voluntary agreement between
the parties for regulating the conduct of political parties and its members etc., during the
process of elections to Assemblies and Parliament. Its legal status is a grey area. After hearing
the views of the officials of the Ministry of Law and considering the problems which have
erupted in the country, from time to time, in the last few years, the Committee feels that the
Code, which was voluntary in nature at one time has not remained so after insertion of para
16A in the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968, which authorises the
Election Commission, to suspend or withdraw the recognition of political parties in case of
violation of Code of Conduct. Besides, some of the paras in the code attract penal provisions
in other laws. [Para 3.17]
9. The Committee further observes that the power of cancellation of registration of a
political party is substantive in nature and, therefore, should not be regulated or provided for
under an “Order” of the Commission. It should either be a part of the Representation of
Peoples, Act 1951 or the Rules framed thereunder. Further, the scope of Article 324 also needs
to be examined as, many of the aspects which should have been covered under the Rules
framed under R.P. Act 1951 are presently covered under instructions issued under Article 324
of the Constitution by the Commission. [Para 3.18]
10. Accordingly, in Committee’s view, remedial legal steps are required to be taken in this
regard. [Para 3.19]

Commission to take all-out effort for 100% EPIC coverage of the States in a time-bound

could be strengthened to accomplish the task in the minimum time span. [Para 3.22]
12. The Committee also puts on record it’s appreciation for the transparency that the
Election Commission of India has brought into the electoral system in the country. There has

Central Government has taken to ensure the smooth flow of funds and the plan of the NALSA
in ensuring the successful implementation of it’s proposed programmes. [Para 4.24]
BAR COUNCIL OF INDIA
21. The Committee takes cognizance of the programmes the BCI proposes to take up in
2012-13. It, however, fails to comprehend as to why the actual requirement was not preferred
to the Ministry of Law and Justice for inclusion in the budgetary projections. During the
meeting of the Committee, the representative of the Ministry had assured the BCI that the
Ministry would support if the demands are made. Therefore, the Committee suggests that the
BCI should prefer their actual fund requirement to the Ministry so that the programmes
envisaged by it are carried out in letter and spirit. Accordingly, a detailed demand for the
purpose may be made at the RE stage. The Committee also wishes to point out that the
Ministry has not assigned justifications for the surrenders of Rs.4,11,900 in 2009-10 and
Rs.6,00,000 in 2011-12 and desires that detail justifications for these surrenders may be made
at the time of furnishing Action Taken Replies. [Para 4.30]
22. The Committee expresses disappointment that a proposal as promising as the Directorate
of Legal Education launched by the BCI had to be discontinued before it’s valuable results
could be harvested. It is unfortunate that a scheme already effectuated had to be suspended
due to shortage of funds. The Committee fails to comprehend why the Government did not
accede to the request made by the BCI for sustaining the Directorate of Legal Education. It,

59
therefore, desires that the BCI in conjunction with the Ministry should take a re-look in the
matter and explore how the scheme can be revived. [Para 4.34]
23. The Committee, further expresses that much more contribution from the BCI especially
in the domain of legislative drafting is expected. Therefore, the BCI is recommended to take
concerted efforts in that respect as well. [Para 4.35]
INSTITUTE OF CONSTITUTIONAL AND PARLIAMENTARY STUDIES
24. The presence of incongruity between the ICPS and the Ministry on the issue of sharing
space which, in turn has caused the delay in the construction of building for the use of ICPS
does not find favor with the Committee. It therefore, desires that the matter may be resolved
at the earliest. As regards the grants to the Institute, the Committee is disconcerted that the
information provided to it by the Department of Legal Affairs reflects grant surrender of
Rs.1,25,626 in 2009-10, Rs.3,50,000 in 2010-11 and a total of Rs.10,41,64,000 in 2011-12. On the
other hand, the ICPS claims that sanctioned grants are not released by the Ministry. To that
effect, the Committee recommends that the Ministry should release the sanctioned grants to
the ICPS without delay. [Para 4.39]
INTERNATIONAL CENTRE FOR ALTERNATIVE DISPUTE RESOLUTION (ICADR)
25. The Committee is constrained to point out that, the casual approach of the Department
of Legal Affairs in releasing the grant for the construction of Convention Centre is puzzling.
The Committee understands that out of the total amount of Rs.12.50 crore sanctioned,
Rs.5 crore was released in 2008-09, Rs.3 crore in 2009-10 and Rs.2.25 crore in 2010-11. It
has also been observed that no fund was released in 2011-12 and a token amount of a mere
Rs.1 crore has been earmarked in the budgetary allocation for the financial year 2012-13,
inspite of Rs.2.25 crore pending release. The Committee, therefore, urges the Department
to earmark the amount of Rs.2.25 crore pending release for the ICADR in the RE stage so
as to enable the completion of construction of the Convention Centre as per schedule.
[Para 4.44]
26. The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the ICADR to encourage Government
Departments and PSUs etc. for including Arbitration/Conciliation Clauses of the ICADR in the
Agreements with other parties. The Committee understands that optimum use of the services
of the ICADR would benefit the Centre in generation of its own resources. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Government should take conscious efforts to publicise the
activities of ICADR to encourage more Government Departments and PSUs to refer their
cases to it. [Para 4.47]
INDIAN LAW INSTITUTE
27. The Committee appreciates the infrastructural development envisaged, i.e., the wi-fi net
working of the campus, the 1 gbps link project of Ministry of Human Resource Development, the video
conferencing system, the Biometric Based Attendance Monitoring System, software for e-governance,
etc. and hopes that these will go a long way in enhancing academic exchanges. [Para 4.50]
28. The Committee is, however distressed to note the huge gap between the demand
projected and allocation received. It does not commend that an institute of this high caliber,
with the objectives to cultivate the science of law, promote advanced studies and research in
law, promote improvement of legal education and publish literature relating to law which are

60
vital in the emergence and advancement of the legal domain of the country should be bereft
of sufficient funds to discharge its basic functions. The Committee, therefore recommends that
the Ministry should revise the projections for the ILI and enhance the same so that they are
allocated at least 25% of their demand at the RE stage. [Para 4.51]
29. On the other hand, the Committee would like to be apprised by the ILI the justifications
for the surrenders in the financial years 2009-10, 2010-11 and 2011-12. The Committee is of
the view that huge surrenders reflect the poor spending capacity of the unit, and as such,
spending units should abstain from this. [Para 4.52]
ANALYSIS OF THE BUDGET ESTIMATES OF THE LEGISLATIVE DEPARTMENT
30. The Committee notes the increase in the overall Budgetary allocation to the Department.
The Committee hopes that the increased amount would be sufficient for the activities to be
taken up this year by the Department. [Para 5.4]
OFFICIAL LANGUAGE WING
31. The Committee appreciates the activities being taken up by the official language
wing. The Committee feels the wing should also translate the Bills/Acts in the regional
languages so that the benefit reaches the lower level courts also. The Committee notes, that
the Official Language Wing could not utilise the allocated fund during the last three years.
The Committee desires that the O.L. wing should take appropriate steps for full utilisation
of money. [Para 5.6]
THE INSTITUTE OF LEGISLATIVE DRAFTING AND RESEARCH
32. The Committee notes that this year also the Department has not taken  any initiative
neither to acquire the land with the Ministry of Urban Affairs nor with the ILDR for
construction of building for ILDR. Such an important Institution like ILDR needs its own
building with adequate infrastructure facilities to carry out its activities. The Committee hopes
the Department will take the issue seriously so that ILDR has its own building during this
year. [Para 5.9]
LEGISLATURE MEASURES UNDERTAKEN BY THE DEPARTMENT ON OFFICE OF PROFIT
33. The Committee appreciates the work done by the Department on the issue of “Office
of Profit” which needs proper definition. The Committee hopes that the Department will take
appropriate steps to get the Bill introduced in the Parliament as early as possible. [Para 5.12]
VOTING RIGHT TO NON- RESIDENT CITIZENS OF INDIA
34. The Committee appreciates the initiatives taken by the Department in facilitating the
voting right to Non-resident citizens of India and also the simplification of submission of
application for registration accompanied by self-attested copies of passport, visa, etc., instead
of getting it attested by the Indian Mission abroad. [Para 5.17]
CENTRALLY SPONSORED SCHEME RELATING TO INFRASTRUCTURAL FACILITIES FOR
THE JUDICIARY
35. The Committee appreciates the revision of the funding pattern of the CSS to 75:25

61
(90:10 for North-East States) and hopes that it will encourage the States to come up with more
proposals for infrastructural development. It, however, wishes to point out that the pendency
of utilisation certificates as reflected in the Ministry’s Outcome Budget (2012-13) is disturbing.
The very fact that there are pending UCs of projects as old as 2002-03 reflects the apathy of
the Ministry in its monitoring of the physical progress made by the States. The Committee,
therefore, urges the Ministry to actively pursue the States on their utilisation of the funds.
The Ministry should also look into the causes of timely and non-submissions of UCs to evolve
a way to plug the shortfall. [Para 6.14]
36. It has also been observed that there exists vast disparity in the pattern of fund release.
The Committee appreciates that the requirement of the States are not the same. However, the
Committee is of the view that a fact-finding exercise is needed to assess the scope and extent
of infrastructural enhancement in States. Accordingly, it recommends that the Ministry should
explore ways of carrying out such an exercise. Furthermore, the Committee desires that those
States/UTs who have not made proposals for infrastructural development of the subordinate
Courts in their State/UT, such as, Bihar, Punjab, Daman & Diu and Lakshadweep may be
pursued and encouraged to avail the Scheme. [Para 6.15]
NATIONAL MISSION FOR JUSTICE DELIVERY AND LEGAL REFORMS
(ii) Setting up of Model Courts (Phase-I)
37. The Committee welcomes the new instrument of service, namely, “National Mission for
Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms” which is aimed at tackling major core problematic issues
of Judiciary. The Committee is appreciative that the scheme has been designed to ensure the
much needed co-ordination between the executive and the judiciary, which, it is certain will
result in a much more efficient delivery of justice in the country. [Para 6.24]
38. The Committee is given to understand through the Outcome Budget (2012-13) of the
Ministry that no timeline has been fixed for the implementation of this Scheme. It is, however,
of the view that it is pertinent to impose timeline in the Action Plan on certain aspects of the
Scheme, such as, setting up of Project Management Units, consultation with stakeholders or
proposed studies on the various aspects of the judicial reforms. The Committee feels that the
experience with many Schemes launched by the Government face set-backs after its
implementation for two or three years due to absence of a strict timeline and ends up clogged
in logjams of non-receipt of UCs and thereafter leading to unutilised funds. The same has been
in the case with the schemes of setting up of Family Courts, Gram Nyayalayas and the projects
under the Centrally Sponsored Schemes. Therefore, the Committee recommends that clear
targets and timelines may be drawn and very close monitoring and regular appraisal should be
made to ensure the successful implementation of the Scheme. [Para 6.25]
ACTION RESEARCH AND STUDIES ON JUDICIAL REFORMS
39. The Committee appreciates that the Department recognises the need for action research
for policy initiatives and judicial reforms measures, effect of pendency reduction drives and the
impact of grants provided by the 13
th Finance Commission. The Committee however, feels that
since the Department has contemplated commissioning of these schemes to already established
organisations, it recommends that such research work may be assigned to organisations under
its administrative control, i.e. ILI, NJA, etc. and the allocation for the purpose also be
reflected in their allocation so as to avoid multiplicity of the research work. It further points

62
out that these organisations are already bringing out their publications on various issues of
judicial reforms and conducting various research work in that field. Therefore, the Committee
opines that the commissioning of the work to them would enhance the financial capacity of
the Organisations. Also, their expertise would be utilised to the maximum benefit if the
research work is assigned to them. [Para 6.31]
EXTERNALLY AIDED PROJECT: “ACCESS TO JUSTICE FOR THE MARGINALIZED IN INDIA”
Access to Justice Project - Government of India Project (New Scheme)
40. The Committee appreciates the approach of the A2J Project which has focused on
empowerment of people through training the para legal workers of the community and
creating the much needed linkage between Legal Services Authorities and the Civil Society
Organisations. The Committee is however, constrained to point out that throughout the five
financial years of the Eleventh Five Year Plan, the Ministry has not been able to exhaust the
allocations earmarked each year for the project. This is indication that the Government has
a lot of scope for implementation of the project still left and therefore, should take concerted
efforts in expanding its area and scope of operation when initiating the proposed new phase
of the scheme to commence from 2013. The Committee desires that the details of the on-going
project as well as plan of action for the proposed new phase of the project may be furnished
to it at the time of furnishing ATRs. [Para 6.39]
COMPUTERISATION OF DISTRICT AND SUBORDINATE COURTS
e-Courts Mission Mode Project Phase-II (New Scheme)
41. The Committee appreciates the ingenious scheme of e-Courts and is optimistic that it
will help in more efficient management of subordinate courts, reduction in pending cases and
increasing the speed of justice delivery processes. The Committee is however, constrained to
point out that the expenditure of the Ministry in 2008-09 and 2011-12 were way below the
allocation projected. It is of the view that under-utilisation of funds are indicative of not
achieving targets. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should fix timelines
and targets for the States while releasing the funds which would also play parameter for
assessing their progress in implementation of the scheme. [Para 6.45]
42. It has also been observed that the BE (2012-13) of Rs.233.66 crore has been pegged
which is near two times higher than the amount of RE (2011-12) of Rs.115 crore. Mention may
be made here that only roughly two-third of the RE (2011-i2) has been utilised. In that
backdrop, the Committee is apprehensive as to whether the Department has the capacity to
utilise the allocation of Rs.233.66 crore in 2012-13. It, therefore, recommends that a clear
timeline and target may be fixed and the progress of implementation should be closely
monitored so as to avoid time and cost overrun. [Para 6.46]
GRAM NYAYALAYAS
43. The Committee expresses its disappointment that in almost three years of the
implementation of the Act, only 151 Gram Nyayalayas are operational. The Committee is of
the firm belief that setting up of Gram Nyayalayas is the answer to providing access to justice
to citizens at their door steps. Therefore, it recommends that the Ministry should take all-out
efforts to root out the hindrances affecting their setting up by States. The Committee is given
to understand that some States have requested for higher central assistance. It therefore, feels

63
that the Ministry should explore the plausibility of enhancing the Central assistance for setting
up of Gram Nyayalayas. [Para 6.51]
44. Furthermore, the Committee desires that the Ministry should make a serious
consideration of the drawbacks and challenges in the setting of Gram Nyayalayas as stated by
the Secretary (Justice). Accordingly, feasibility of enhancement of funds may be explored so
that the States may augment the requisite infrastructur e. [Para 6.52 ]
FAMILY COURTS
45. The Committee assumes that the States not being too keen on setting up Family
Courts is most likely due to their requirement to provide matching share of Rs.10 lakh per
court. It therefore, is of the opinion that the Ministry should endeavour to survey the
apprehensions of the States in setting up of Family Courts and if financial constraint is one
of the cause, it should revise the funding pattern as has been done in the case of Gram
Nyayalayas to encourage more States to come up with proposals. The Committee is of the
strong belief that the setting up of Family Courts will come a long way in reducing pendency
of cases, especially due to the fact that it has been reflected in the Budget Outcome (2012-
13) of the Ministry that 90056 cases were disposed of by Family Courts upto 2009. It also
anticipates a more efficient delivery of justice to the people by setting up of more Family
Courts in the States. Therefore, the Ministry should envisage ensuring setting up of maximum
number of Family Courts across the length and breadth of the country. [Para 6.58]
THIRTEENTH FINANCE COMMISSION
46. The Committee is overwhelmed at the length of efforts taken to streamline justice
delivery. It is however, distressed that the 13th Finance Commission has recommended an
impressive grant of Rs. 5000 crore to be utilised over a period of 2010-15, out of which a mere
Rs. 1353.62 crore has been utilised. This reflects the tardy pace of the Department in its
implementation of schemes. Furthermore, the Committee observes that the States of Chhattisgarh,
Goa, Gujarat, Jharkhand and Meghalaya have not so far utilised grants under this scheme. The
Committee, in this regard desires that the Department may furnish the justification for such
absence of proposals to it while submitting its ATRs. It further recommends that the Department
should beef up monitoring of schemes while encouraging more States to come up with proposals
under this scheme. At the time of sending ATRs to this Report, the Committee would like to
be apprised of the steps taken in this aspect and the outcome thereof. [Para 6.61]
NON PLAN SCHEMES
NATIONAL JUDICIAL ACADEMY
47. In this backdrop, the Committee notes the information given by the Director, National
Judicial Academy and desires that the Academy should take up the role and have the objective
to educate and train judges and help them make judicious judgments in courts to create a
healthy civil society. [Para 6.67]
V ACANCIES IN SUPREME COURT AND HIGH COURTS
48. An appraisal of the vacancy position of Judges in both Supreme Court and High Courts
as provided by the Department is disheartening. One major factor affecting these vacancies
appears to be the procedure of appointment and the current proactive of the collegium system

64
also raises apprehensions. The Committee, therefore, is of the view that the whole system of
appointment of judges calls for a review and rehaul. It is of the firm belief that once the
process of appointment is set right, other related issues, such as court management and
pendency of cases will fall in place. The Department is, accordingly exhorted to take efficacious
steps in this domain. [Para 6.71]
49. While deliberating on the vacancies in the higher judiciary and the long time taken in
the disposal of cases pending before the courts, the Committee pointed out the feasibility of
having an All India Judicial Service. In response, the Secretary, Department of Justice
informed the Committee that a proposal is presently under Government’s consideration and is
in the channel for consideration by the Committee of Secretaries. [Para 6.72]
50. The Committee feels that there is a shortage of judges at all levels, be it in the higher
judiciary or in the subordinate courts and this is one of the major factors for delay in the
adjudication of cases. Shortage of judges is also a major constraint for setting up of new
courts. The Committee appreciates and welcomes idea of having in place an All India Judicial
Service but, in case, certain States have issues in this proposal, the Committee feels that the
Central Government can at least make a beginning by holding an examination for recruiting
judges 
at the all India level, covering S tates that agr ee to par ticipate or  accept candidates
selected on the basis of the said recruitment. The Committee feels such a move would ensure
an all time availability of qualified and deserving candidates for appointment in subordinate
courts. [Para 6.73]
DEMAND NO. 64 : SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
51. The Committee is not in agreement with the Ministry and the opinion of the Chief
Justice of India as well. The Committee feels that unwillingness regarding establishment of the
other Benches of the Supreme Court cannot be justified on the grounds that it would attract
a cumbersome process of constitutional amendment. The Committee also feels that such an
amendment is the need of the hour and would prove to be a step in the right direction to
make the Higher Courts accessible to all the regions of the country. The Committee feels that
the Constitution of India is a living document and has enough scope to accommodate the
demands arising out in a changed milieu in view of the provisions under Article 130 that read–
“The Supreme Court sits in Delhi. It can, however, meet in any other place or places as
the Chief Justice may, with the approval of the President.” [Para 7.2]
52. The Committee, therefore, reiterates the need for establishment of benches of the
Supreme Court as it would be of immense help to the poor who cannot afford to travel from
their native places to Delhi. [Para 7.3]
53. The Committee appreciates that the Ministry has replied in affirmative and forwarded
the abovementioned Committee’s recommendations to the Supreme Court Registry for necessary
action. The Committee hopes that the Supreme Court Registry would positively take decisions
in this regard. [Para 7.5]
54. The Committee is pleased to note that the Department is in agreement with the
Committee’s recommendation regarding enabling the Supreme Court and High Courts to
generate Revenue themselves which can also be utilised by the Subordinate Judiciary. The
Committee would, however, appreciate if the Department pursues the matter with the Department
of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance and the State Governments to consider the matter
expeditiously. The Committee may be apprised their feedback, accordingly. [Para 7.7]

65
PENDENCY OF CASES
55. The Committee expresses it serious concerns over the huge pendency of cases in
Higher Courts. Taking into account the reasons cited by the Registrar, Supreme Court in this
regard, the Committee feels that the problem is not being addressed seriously and wholehearted
efforts are yet to be made to deal with the problem. The Committee is of the view that both
Executive and Judiciary should work in tandem to deal with the adversities arising out of
mounting pendency. As far as the need of more judges is concerned, the Committee reiterates
its earlier recommendation that the vacancies of judges in the High Court should be expeditiously
filled up. The Government should vigorously pursue the matter with the Chief Justice of the
High Courts for necessary actions. [Para 7.9]

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel,
Public Grievances, Law and Justice, having been authorised by the Committee on its behalf, do hereby
present the Fifty Third Report on the Right of Citizens for Time Bound Delivery of Goods and
Services and Redressal of their Grievances Bill, 2011. The Bill seeks to establish a mechanism to lay
down an obligation upon every public authority to publish citizens charter stating therein the time
within which specified goods shall be supplied and services be rendered and provide for a grievance
redressal mechanism for non-compliance of citizens charter and for matters connected therewith or
incidental thereto.
2. In pursuance of the rules relating to the Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee,
the Hon’ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha referred

20th December, 2011 and pending therein, to this Committee on the 13 th January, 2012 for examination
and report.

to solicit views/suggestions from desirous individuals/organisations on the provisions of the Bill.

to which memoranda containing suggestions were received, from various organizations/ individuals/
experts, by the Committee.

18th July, 2012.

placed before it :–
